protocolRevision:
PROTOCOL REVISION (user-approved; record it verbatim in the round's receipts):
- Each Kotoba workload w runs n_w = LSF_w · 8192 · m_w iterations, with m_w ∈ {1,2,4,8,16}. Reported ratio_w = (4/m_w) · K_ns / C_ns. The full-19 GM is over those ratios.
- m_w is fixed BEFORE transfer from local data only, never adjusted after any Joseph timing. Write it into a pre-registration receipt (hashed) in s3. Rule: m_w = the smallest power of two such that the projected Joseph interval ≥ 1.0 s, using the conservative Joseph/local ratio 0.33 (local_elapsed · m_w · 0.33 ≥ 1.0 s), subject to fuel: (benchmarkFuel + verifyFuel)(n_w) must stay well under 2^35 (≤ ~0.9 · 2^35). If fuel binds, take the largest feasible m_w and report the projection.
- Unchanged: the C arm (GSF 32768, frozen round65 binaries); the 0.5 s floor; fuel 2^35; the trusted loader; warm1/sample1; ≤3 CPU-only retries; first qualified; no subset GM.
- Arena caps (KEXE_* env): raise only where the new n needs it (e.g. qrduino KEXE_PAIRS 65536 vs 40960·m pairs, slre pairs, aha vectors), and record every change.
- Expected exactness values (benchmarkFuel, verifyFuel, result, the 17-counter arena line) must be re-derived for each new n from a TRUSTED reference, never from the candidate m92 itself. Use the same method that produced expected-original-accounting.json, or something at least as independent. If fuel/arena are exactly linear in n, show it from ≥2 reference n values per workload. Tell me what reference you used.
- Add the local short-interval screen to s3: refuse to transfer if any workload's projected Joseph interval at its m_w is < 0.75 s.

PROTOCOL AMENDMENT 1 (coordinator decision, before any pre-registration; replaces the local-wall-time projection, the 0.33 ratio and the 0.75 s screen):
1) LOCAL IDLE GATE: drop it for pre-registration. This machine carries persistent unrelated load (java pid 73536, hermes, Codex, node), which I'm not allowed to kill, so ≥70% idle may never happen. Local wall time under load is meaningless anyway. Use a deterministic, load-independent projection instead.
P_w(m) = I_w · m / R_w, where:
- I_w = the candidate's instruction count for w at m=1 (local, deterministic: the instr= values your s3/validate runs record);
- R_w = the FASTEST Joseph instructions-per-second observed for w in any previous round (m43 17 workloads, m87 6 incl. matmult's short attempt). Use the instruction count of that exact prior image (recount locally if needed);
- if w has no prior Joseph data, R_w = 30e9 instr/s.
Fastest R gives the shortest projection, so the rule is conservative for the floor. Calibration comes only from earlier rounds, never from this round, so pre-registration stays clean. Record the R_w table and its sources in the pre-registration receipt.
2) SELECTION AND SCREEN (replaces my 0.33-ratio and 0.75 s rules):
- m_w = the smallest power of two in {1,2,4,8,16} with P_w(m_w) ≥ 1.0 s, capped by fuel ≤ 0.9·2^35.
- Retime rule: if (image, n_w) was already timed on Joseph (aha-mont64, crc32 and matmult-int at m=1 in m87), take the next feasible power of two instead. That makes aha-mont64 m ≥ 2 and needs its KEXE_VECTORS/VECTOR_ITEMS caps doubled; record it.
- Screen: refuse transfer if any P_w(m_w) < 0.6 s.
- Example: matmult-int at m=8 projects 1.49e9·8/12.4e9 ≈ 0.96 s using its identical m87 image's own Joseph rate.
